comment: The apps channel of the sessions of one project. The IDE opens it with userApps false and the base environment of its processes, so the channel holds the project entries only. ${home} has an app file of the user with the id of the project entry, which the channel never reads. The step file {path, text} writes a file, appStart {command} expects air-ide to start the process, and appExit {code, stderr} ends it. The lines of stderr come before the exit, and clock {advanceMs} moves the clock of the backoff. The lines of the link app are the stdin and the stdout of that process.

comment: appsOpen with userApps false opens the apps channel of the sessions. Each process gets the base environment in place of the environment of the IDE process, without each PATH. The snapshot holds the project entry vcs and no app of the user.

Always Allow of the command that the banner of the places showed, and the answer of the banner of a session, which names the agent too. The scan reads the code of the entry and of its argument file app.ts, since the user answered its command.

A restart starts the project entry, since it starts on its first view and has none. The fingerprint covers the executable and app.ts. The start logs one info entry. A project entry is a plain MCP server: its initialize offers no x-air-app, the app answers with none, and the link lists its tools.

comment: An agent calls the tool status of the running entry. A check compares the marks of the run with the files now, and no file changed, so the call reaches the app.

Another file takes the path of the script app.ts, and no file of the registry changes. The next agent call sees the new mark of app.ts and parks behind one scan. The scan reads another fingerprint, so the consent is unknown, and the process stops before the call reaches the app. The call sets the consent request r1 of its session, and its error names it.

The user allows the changed script with the agent. The scan of the call before read its code, so the answer holds at once. The answer names no request, so the entry starts on no view, and it ends the request r1 of its target.
The local registry is no JSON object, so it does not parse, and the scan logs one warn. The file keeps the apps of its last good content.
